name: Advanced Concepts of Distributed Databases - Programming Database Web Applications (IN2140)

reviews.comment: The course is pretty cool! you can work on your own idea for a fun project. You basically create a modern data-driven web app. It's lots of fun, and you can learn new tools and frameworks. If you convince your friends, you can work with them as a team!

name: Advanced Deep Learning for Computer Vision: Visual Computing (IN2390)

reviews.comment:
Lecture: The course is pretty small (~30 people). Thus, lectures are very interactive and covers very recent progressions in the CV domain.

Project/Exam: Oral exam is mainly asking for facts from the slides, projects are graded pretty strictly and need ~8h/week during the semester. 

Grading: The subject is graded based on a project (60%) and an oral exam (40%). Despite a preselection of people who had <= 1.3 in I2DL, only 2 out of 30 participants got a 1.0. However, only 5/30 received a grade worse than 2.0.
Much workload. 50/50 project grade and exam grade. Content of the lecture is insane when taking the project into account. Content-wise much overlapping with other ML lectures.

Lecture: Divided into 7 blocks held by the PhD students of Prof. Groh (not himself!) => Varying quality of the lectures: Most were motivated to give high-quality lecture, but some lectures were just bad due to lacking lecturing experience: Pacing through difficult topics without giving proper explanations, unstructured or messy explanations.
Overall, the lectures were quite nice (4/5 stars). The topics were closer to the state-of-the-art of LLMs than in any other class I have ever taken.

Exercise: Provided Jupyter notebooks to code on your own (~3h each) + discussed in a central exercise. Very high-level. Did not go into details, but I guess that would just be impossible in a reasonable time frame.

Exam: It was fair. It was not the easiest, but if you understood and remembered the concepts from class, you were well-prepared to do well. There is a lot of material, though, and every block has a little bit of its own style.

name: Advanced Seminar Course for Graduands and Postgraduates (IN2122)

reviews.comment:

Exercises: Exercises were really bad imo. Explanations were limited to reading out sample solutions + they replied to none of the questions posted in Moodle. They didn't formulate expectations for the exam transparently. 

Exam: In SS2024, the exam was very different from the ones in the past. If you knew what to prepare for, it would have been manageable but since it was very different from past exams, it was rather challenging. However, the curve was generous.

name: Practical Course: Open Source Lab (IN0012, IN2106, IN4308)

reviews.comment: You can contribute to any open source software you want, and give weekly updates in a video call. Most people got 1,3 or 1,0. The "lecture material" is mostly a git tutorial.
I recommend to refresh your knowledge of linear algebra before taking this course :)

The lecture can be slow at times, but overall it's nice that the lecturer takes time to explain things. 

1st half of the lecture is about concepts of motion planning for mobile robots on a high level of abstractions: It's mostly about intuitions and algorithm ideas - no deep details.

2nd half is about sensor output filtering and data fusion (namely Kalman Filter, Extended Kalman Filter, Unscented Kalman Filter, Particle Filter, Bayes Filter). It's more math-heavy but still the main goal is to gain intuitions of what the filters do, and understand their core principles - no need to learn details by heart.

Overall, I liked the course for teaching the high-level ideas - something often missed in other classes.

Lectures: The professor is interactive during his lectures but doesn't have a clearly structured slide set. Often times he finds himself lost in what he wanted to explain. However, content is rather redundant with modules from the mechanical engineering bachelor's. 

Exercises: Exercises are exam-style questions and much more important than the lecture to pass the course successfully. The TA was explaining things pretty clearly. 

Exam: Exams can contain mistakes and are very tough to solve in the given time period. The curve is generous and ~80/130pts. are required for a 1.0.
